strokeOrder: draw the left vertical from top to bottom, then without lifting turn and flick up to the right
lift, draw the bar from left to right
lift, begin above the bar and draw the vertical down through it, then without lifting loop round to the left and back up, cross the vertical and run out to the lower right
lift, draw the small circle of the handakuten clockwise, starting and ending at its foot
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03071 file records ぱ as four stroke paths in this order and direction: は's three strokes (the left vertical with its flick, the bar and the vertical with its loop), then the handakuten, one small circle drawn clockwise from its foot; so there are three pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03071.svg, hiragana ぱ (U+3071 HIRAGANA LETTER PA), four stroke paths kvg:03071-s1 to s4 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s3 are は's strokes, the same paths as in its file for は, kanji/0306f.svg; s4 is the handakuten, one closed ring that starts at its foot and runs clockwise, round the left side, over the top and down the right side back to the foot. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick.

notes: は with the handakuten, read pa. The third sign of いっぱい and of しんぱい.
